document.title: Reagan Letter to Gandhi
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Reply to Gandhi's January 7 letter. Reagan announces positive decisions on a supercomputer, INSAT 1-D and LCA, expresses skepticism that Soviet national reconciliation is anything but preserving Najibullah, and promises to press Pakistan on its nuclear program.

key_claims: Reagan said Soviet reconciliation plans mainly aimed to preserve the Najibullah regime.
Reagan said Soviet and DRA forces were violating the Pakistan border at unprecedented levels in 1987.
The US said it sought no strategic advantage in Afghanistan and would back an agreement ensuring full Soviet withdrawal consistent with UN resolutions.
Reagan asked India to press the Soviets on Afghanistan.
The US said it would keep pressing Pakistan on its nuclear programme while urging India to consider Zia's proposals.
